headline: Anti-drug campaigner man set on fire dies in Mymensingh
summary: Farhad Hossain, a 35-year-old vegetable seller and social activist, died at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital after being attacked by unidentified assailants.
details: Farhad Hossain, a 35-year-old man, died today after being allegedly set on fire by unidentified assailants in the Madhyahisya area of Muktagacha town, Mymensingh.
The attack occurred around 10:00 pm on Wednesday night. Assailants allegedly poured petrol on him from behind and set him ablaze before fleeing the scene.
Locals rescued him and rushed him to the Muktagacha Upazila Health Complex, before he was later referred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH), where he died around noon today.
Farhad was a vegetable seller by profession and was known for his active involvement in social movements, including campaigns against drugs and demands for employment opportunities.
His father, Abdus Sattar, believes the attack was linked to his son's anti-drug campaigns and social activities.
Police have launched an investigation to identify the perpetrators. The body has been sent to the Mymensingh Medical College morgue for an autopsy.
According to the officer-in-charge of Muktagacha Police Station, no case has been filed and no arrests have been made so far.
caption:
A 35-year-old anti-drug campaigner was allegedly set on fire and killed in Mymensingh.

Farhad Hossain, a 35-year-old man, died today after being allegedly set on fire by unidentified assailants in the Madhyahisya area of Muktagacha town, Mymensingh.

The attack occurred around 10:00 pm on Wednesday night. Assailants allegedly poured petrol on him from behind and set him ablaze before fleeing the scene.

Locals rescued him and rushed him to the Muktagacha Upazila Health Complex, before he was later referred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH), where he died around noon today.

Farhad was a vegetable seller by profession and was known for his active involvement in social movements, including campaigns against drugs and demands for employment opportunities.

His father, Abdus Sattar, believes the attack was linked to his son's anti-drug campaigns and social activities.

Police have launched an investigation to identify the perpetrators. The body has been sent to the Mymensingh Medical College morgue for an autopsy.

According to the officer-in-charge of Muktagacha Police Station, no case has been filed and no arrests have been made so far.

headline: Law and order visibly improved in Bangladesh, says Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced strategic plans for further improvement and highlighted anti-drug operations and security measures in Parliament.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told Parliament on Thursday that there has been visible progress in the country's law and order situation since the current government took office.
The minister stated that short, medium, and long-term strategic plans have been adopted to further improve the security situation and ensure the safety of people's lives and property.

He noted that the Bangladesh Police have intensified their efforts to curb crimes such as murder, snatching, and kidnapping, while working to restore the morale of the police force following the July revolution.

Addressing queries, the minister revealed that 60,598 anti-drug operations were conducted nationwide from February 17 to August 31, 2026, resulting in 18,040 cases and the arrest of 18,858 drug traffickers.

On the security of the capital, the minister mentioned a project called 'Development of Smart Policing in DMP' to bring the entire Dhaka Metropolitan area under CCTV monitoring, which is currently undergoing DPP restructuring.
Regarding the BDR mutiny, the minister clarified that 6,286 people were dismissed and 2,510 were given compulsory retirement following legal processes, and there is no scope for their reinstatement.
Additionally, the Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury provided data on river erosion, stating that an average of 3,500 families and 15,000 people are displaced annually.
The Finance Minister also shared labor force data from the 2024 survey, stating that the total labor force is 71.71 million, with a unemployment rate of 3.66%.
caption:
Law and order in Bangladesh has visibly improved, according to Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told Parliament on Thursday that there has been visible progress in the country's law and order situation since the current government took office.

The minister stated that short, medium, and long-term strategic plans have been adopted to further improve the security situation and ensure the safety of people's lives and property.

He noted that the Bangladesh Police have intensified their efforts to curb crimes such as murder, snatching, and kidnapping, while working to restore the morale of the police force following the July revolution.

Addressing queries, the minister revealed that 60,598 anti-drug operations were conducted nationwide from February 17 to August 31, 2026, resulting in 18,040 cases and the arrest of 18,858 drug traffickers.

On the security of the capital, the minister mentioned a project called 'Development of Smart Policing in DMP' to bring the entire Dhaka Metropolitan area under CCTV monitoring, which is currently undergoing DPP restructuring.

Regarding the BDR mutiny, the minister clarified that 6,286 people were dismissed and 2,510 were given compulsory retirement following legal processes, and there is no scope for their reinstatement.

Additionally, the Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury provided data on river erosion, stating that an average of 3,500 families and 15,000 people are displaced annually.

The Finance Minister also shared labor force data from the 2024 survey, stating that the total labor force is 71.71 million, with a unemployment rate of 3.66%.
